sections.name: GeoJsonPosition, GeoJsonLinearRing, GeoJsonPolygon, GeoJsonMultiPolygon, ParcelGeoJson
sections.title: Map shape formats
sections.what: Defines how a parcel's outline is written: a single shape or a group of shapes, each made of coordinate pairs in longitude and latitude. It also lists where a geometry came from and how reliable it is.
sections.why: A common shape format lets map tools read parcels from different sources.
sections.watch_out: A ring of points must close on its first point. Code that builds shapes must make sure it does.

sections.name: ParcelGeometry
sections.title: Stored parcel geometry
sections.what: Describes a stored parcel shape with its ids, its geometry, the coordinate system, where it came from, its quality, and when it was created and updated.
sections.why: Storing the source and quality with the shape lets the screens say how much to trust it.
sections.watch_out: The khesra id is optional, so code must not assume every parcel has one.

sections.name: CalculatedGeometryArea, ParcelAreaSourceType, ParcelAreaAvailability
sections.title: Area in several units
sections.what: Describes a calculated area in square metres, hectares and acres, and marks that it was calculated from the shape rather than typed in.
sections.why: Showing all three units lets the screens compare areas written in different units.
sections.watch_out: The three numbers must describe the same area. Changing one without the others would make them disagree.

sections.name: ParcelAreaSource, ParcelAreaComparisonStatus
sections.title: One area source and its status
sections.what: Describes one source of an area, such as a historical record, a survey record or a shape calculation, with its raw value, unit, value in acres, whether it is available, and where it is referenced. Also lists the four possible comparison outcomes.
sections.why: Keeping each source's raw value and its acres value lets someone see exactly how the conversion was made.
sections.watch_out: The raw value and acres value can be empty when a source is unavailable, so code must not treat them as zero.

sections.name: ParcelAreaPairwiseComparison
sections.title: Comparison between two sources
sections.what: Describes the result of comparing two area sources: the two sides, the difference in acres, the percentage difference, the status, which policy was used, and an explanation key.
sections.why: A pair-by-pair comparison shows exactly which records disagree.
sections.watch_out: The difference fields can be empty, and a zero difference must not be confused with a missing value.

sections.name: ParcelAreaComparisonPolicy
sections.title: Comparison policy thresholds
sections.what: Holds the percentage limits for calling two areas consistent or worth reviewing, plus a legal disclaimer saying the check is only a demonstration.
sections.why: Keeping the thresholds in one named policy makes the judgment visible and easy to change.
sections.watch_out: The thresholds are demonstration values. Changing them changes every verdict, so record any change.

sections.name: ParcelAreaComparisonSummary
sections.title: Summary of the comparison
sections.what: Gives a summary key that names the overall finding, such as areas closely aligned or review recommended, along with the status behind it.
sections.why: A single summary lets the home page show one clear finding without reading every pair.
sections.watch_out: The summary key and status must agree with the pairwise results, or the screen will show a contradiction.

sections.name: ParcelIntelligence
sections.title: Full parcel intelligence bundle
sections.what: Gathers everything known about one parcel into one shape: its geometry, calculated area, historical and survey areas, all the sources, all the comparisons, the summary and the policy.
sections.why: One bundle lets a single request return the whole picture for a parcel.
sections.watch_out: The geometry and calculated area can be empty, so the screen must handle a parcel with no shape.

summary: Defines the shapes for parcel map geometry, the area calculated from it, and the comparison of areas from different records.
purpose: Describes parcel shapes in standard map coordinates, the areas from each source, the pairwise comparisons, and the policy thresholds used to judge them.
why: Comparing areas from several sources needs one clear structure. Likely reason: the app checks whether records agree. Reason not stated in the code.
how: The file defines GeoJSON shapes for polygons, the parcel geometry record with its source and quality, the calculated area in several units, each area source, pairwise comparisons, the policy thresholds, a summary, and the full parcel intelligence bundle.
inputs: None directly. Other code fills these shapes.
outputs: None directly. The labels guide the checker and the screens.
risks: Two type names, the provenance and source type, have the same values. Changing one without the other could confuse code that uses both.
debug: If an area comparison looks wrong, check the threshold numbers in the policy and confirm the units are acres.
